messages:
zoe: Thinking out loud — we should move from a single global token pool to per-queue token prioritization + a light regional fairshare layer. Goal: preserve interactive latency while still letting background/batch jobs drain in low-cost regions.

rahul: concrete ask — how do we compute per-queue refill and burst? any simple formula we can start canary with?

zoe: proposal sketch: each queue Q gets base_refill_rps * queue_weight[Q] * regional_factor. burst credits granted up to burst_cap_per_queue and replenished at a slower rate. regional_factor is a running window of free capacity in the region (0..1).

zoe: example config (human-readable):
```
queue_weights:
  interactive: 0.7
  background: 0.2
  batch: 0.1
refill_rps: 1200  # global baseline tokens/sec
burst_credits: 5000  # global pool apportioned by weight
spill_to_fallback_pct: 0.10  # allowed spill if region saturated
```

evan: spill rules: allow up to `spill_to_fallback_pct` of requests to route to fallback region if local fairshare < 0.05, but only if cost delta < configured threshold. need telemetry for cross-region token transfers so we can bill and cap.

lina: add these metrics: `tokens_available_per_queue`, `tokens_burn_rps_per_queue`, `regional_fairshare_ratio`, `burst_usage_per_tenant`. add alert when 99p burst_usage > 80% for >5m.

rahul: edge case — preemptible GPU eviction causing large token underflow (we lose ability to service and tokens keep draining). Do we smear tokens back after reconciliation or immediately stall admission?

zoe: prefer immediate local admission throttle + mark region as degraded. reconciliation job should credit back tokens slowly to avoid sudden surge. e.g. refill_backoff = max(1, eviction_rate*2) seconds per refill step.

sre-bot: sim-run: per-queue weights 0.7/0.2/0.1, refill 1200rps -> 98th latency stable for interactive, background throughput drops 22%. Enabling 10% spill to fallback recovers 12% background throughput but increases cost ~9%.

evan: cost tradeoff is acceptable if we can pin which tenants opt-in to spill. default = opt-out. Also cap per-tenant burst credits to avoid noisy neighbors.

rahul: can we compute conservative starting numbers automatically? maybe sample 24h token burn per-queue and set queue_weight = interactive_burn / total_burn * smoothing_factor. smoothing_factor = 0.6 to avoid flipping.

lina: will add dashboards and an evaluation job: run two 30m stress sims (normal + preemptible-eviction pattern) and export `tokens_burn_rps_per_queue` and `regional_spill_count`.

zoe: action items: 1) rahul + evan implement admission layer changes (config + per-queue metrics) — canary in us-west2 only, 2) lina add dashboards and alerts, 3) run sims and post results here, 4) decide tenant spill opt-in policy after cost telemetry.

rahul: ack, starting a branch today. will post a short PR description and a small local sim tool.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for us-west2/admission-v2 at 03:30 UTC.

zoe: nice. small note — keep mutation of `queue_weights` behind feature flag; we'll want rapid rollback if 99p latency regresses. :thumbsup:
